page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 237 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates moderate performance across memory and database workloads, alongside weaker compute-heavy results. The instance achieves average performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and PassMark database operations, which scored 2599.67. Large-block memory bandwidth is also average, reaching 71.58 GB/sec for read-only and 34.94 GB/sec for write operations. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 6052.47 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3208.0. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, but the processor lacks AVX or AMX instruction sets, contributing to poor performance in LLM inference and bzip3 decompression.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6gd.xlarge offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive applications that benefit from local, low-latency NVMe storage without requiring high-end compute power. The combination of 32.0 GB of RAM and local SSD storage makes this instance well-suited for caching layers, medium-sized databases, and memory-bound data processing tasks. It is less optimal for compute-bound workloads, multi-threaded compilation, or machine learning inference due to its lower multi-core efficiency and lack of specialized vector instructions.
